# The shift from sequential monotherapy to single-pill combinations

The Indian Society of Hypertension published a consensus guideline for the
management of hypertension in 2025. International guidance over the preceding
decade has moved consistently in one direction: away from starting on a single
agent and titrating upward, and towards **initiating combination therapy
early**, usually as a single-pill fixed-dose combination, on the grounds of
faster control and materially better adherence.

## Why this matters for prioritisation

This is the clinical mechanism behind a pattern that is directly observable in
the supplied dataset: dual and triple fixed-dose combinations growing faster
than the plain molecules they are built from.

The strategic reading is that the growth in combination sub-segments is not a
transient marketing effect that will mean-revert. It is guideline-aligned
substitution of one prescription for two, and substitution of that kind tends
to persist. It supports projecting continued outperformance for combination
archetypes over a three-to-five-year horizon rather than assuming reversion to
the therapy-area rate.

Confidence is set to medium because the guideline is recent and Indian
prescribing practice adopts guidance with a lag; the dataset evidence for the
shift is stronger than the guideline citation alone.
